subject.title: fix(security): add default pidsLimit for sandbox containers

question: Should Docker sandbox containers enforce a default PID ceiling for existing configs, and what validated opt-out should remain for workloads that need Docker default or unlimited behavior?
rationale: The change improves containment but alters a security-sensitive runtime default and the current schema/runtime/docs contract does not preserve a clear opt-out.

options.title: Enforce with opt-out
options.body: Keep the default PID ceiling, but first align schema, docs, and tests so an explicit opt-out and positive overrides are valid and documented.

options.title: Keep operator-only limits
options.body: Leave omitted `pidsLimit` as Docker default behavior and instead document or audit-recommend explicit resource limits.

options.title: Pause for resource policy
options.body: Hold this one-field default until PID, CPU, memory, and recreate behavior are decided as one sandbox resource-limit policy.

recommendation.title: Enforce with opt-out
recommendation.body: Keep the default PID ceiling, but first align schema, docs, and tests so an explicit opt-out and positive overrides are valid and documented.

likelyOwner.reason: The current sandbox config/schema surfaces that need the policy alignment were recently introduced by this owner path.
